office_does: The assessor values every parcel in the county for property tax, runs the exemption and current-use programs, and computes levy rates and puts the taxes on the roll.
race_blurb: Incumbent Kelly Todd Mauck, elected in 2022 as a Republican and now running with no party preference, faces Doug Stults (Prefers Democratic Party), a residential appraiser on his own staff who led the primary 52.7% to 47.1%. The race centers on Mauck's $5.6 million levy reduction to return school-levy overcollections, which the Department of Revenue disputes.

candidates.summary: Residential appraiser in the Island County Assessor's Office for more than 4.5 years, with two IAAO designations and no elected record; endorsed by former Assessor Bernie Upchurch and the Island County Democrats.
highlights: Taxpayer Protection Plan would test every levy before he signs the roll, so a rate carried over from last year is caught [S5]
Wants refund checks to the people who paid the levy overcollection, not credits on later tax bills [S5]
Would make no large levy correction without a written Department of Revenue determination first [S5]
Pledges a public conflict-of-interest log, posted work hours and IAAO certification for the office [S4]
Led the August primary with 52.7% of the vote [S12]

taxes.basis: Runs a 'Taxpayer Protection Plan' to return every overcharged dollar to those who paid it and to widen exemption enrollment; no position on tax levels themselves.

experience.basis: Never elected and challenging his own office's elected head, though he brings 4.5 years of appraisal work inside the office and national IAAO credentials.

candidates.summary: Island County Assessor since 2023 and former county undersheriff, running with no party preference; endorsed by all three county commissioners, most of the state's elected assessors and the Island County Republican Party.
highlights: Cut the 2025 state school levy by $5.6 million to return 2022 and 2024 overcollections; the Department of Revenue disputes most of it [S7]
Says he will go to court rather than raise a later levy to undo the correction [S7]
Says the office now meets all eight Department of Revenue standards, up from four in 2023 [S6]
Says the office has run under budget and cut unnecessary staffing costs [S4]
Supported the 2026 law raising income limits for the senior, disabled and veteran exemption [S8]

taxes.basis: Lowered the 2025 levy to refund overcollections, says he would refuse a state demand to raise a later levy, and backed the wider senior exemption.

spending.basis: Says the office has consistently run under budget, reduced unnecessary staffing costs and created efficiencies.

experience.basis: First-term incumbent running on his record in office, after 22 years in county law enforcement including undersheriff, backed by the sitting commissioners and 28 elected assessors.
